title: Open-world champions: one named monster per region
prompt: A sheet of seven blocky voxel champion monsters, each bigger and more decorated than the ordinary kind and shown beside a small Percy outline for scale, from the high three-quarter game angle: Bronzebeak, a huge Stymphalian bird with razor bronze feathers and a red crest; Shadowfang, a scarred black hellhound with a broken iron collar and smoking eyes; Queen Gale, a storm-grey harpy queen with a crown of feathers and lightning in her talons; the Red King, a crimson giant scorpion with a golden stinger and a crown of spines; the Bronze Warden, a hulking bronze automaton with a single glowing blue eye and a shield; Gorgos, a Cyclops chieftain in bear pelts with a tree-trunk club; and the Pale King, a skeleton king in tarnished armour with a crown and a black sword, green fire in his eyes. Dramatic and fun for ages 8 to 14, never gory. 3D game art in the blocky voxel style of Minecraft Dungeons: characters built from cubes, with a large cube head whose face is simple pixel art (about 8 × 8 pixels: pixel eyes, a pixel mouth, hair drawn as pixels and as a few blocky tufts), a boxy torso, square arms and legs, crisp pixel-art textures (about 16 pixels per block) with simple shading, chunky readable silhouettes; warm cinematic lighting, soft ambient occlusion and glowing magic effects. Costume colours and details follow the Camp Half-Blood cartoon concept art. Palette: camp orange #f28c28, sea teal #0f6f73, deep navy #10233d, jade #2e8b6e, coral #e8664a, bronze gold #c9963a, lightning yellow #ffd84a, parchment cream #f4ead5, vase black #17130f and owl grey #8c96a3. Flat light-grey background. No lettering, logos, captions or watermark.
